# M0-S5 C1: a CC stored with `go env -w` wins over the zig fallback under
# plain `go`. With the fake zig on PATH, the default C compiler hidden, and
# CC configured in the GOENV file, `go build` must use the configured
# compiler (wrapper log non-empty, zig log empty) and `go env CC` must print
# the configured value (never `zig cc`), including with cross GOOS/GOARCH.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
env GOENV=$WORK/go.env
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache

# Install the fake zig and the CC wrapper, and record the real C compiler
# before PATH narrows; both delegate to the recorded path.
chmod 0755 $WORK/fakebin/zig $WORK/ccwrap/cc
exists -exec $WORK/fakebin/zig
exists -exec $WORK/ccwrap/cc
[!GOOS:windows] exec sh -c 'command -v cc || command -v gcc || command -v clang'
[!GOOS:windows] cp stdout $WORK/realcc.txt
env REALPATH=$PATH

# No CC anywhere yet: process env empty, GOENV file fresh. The narrowed
# PATH hides the default C compiler while the fake zig stays findable.
env CC=
env CGO_ENABLED=1
env ZIGLOG=$WORK/zig.log
env CCLOG=$WORK/cc.log
env PATH=$WORK/fakebin:$GOROOT/bin

# Store the wrapper as CC in the GOENV file. The OS environment holds no
# CC, so the write lands without the "does not override" warning.
go env -w CC=$WORK/ccwrap/cc
! stderr 'does not override'

# `go env CC` prints the configured compiler, never the zig fallback.
go env CC
stdout 'ccwrap'
! stdout 'zig cc'

# Same with cross GOOS/GOARCH in effect: no zig triple leaks in.
env GOOS=linux
env GOARCH=arm64
go env CC
stdout 'ccwrap'
! stdout 'zig cc'
env GOOS=
env GOARCH=

# Plain `go build` uses the configured CC: the wrapper log is non-empty,
# the binary runs, and the fake zig never runs.
[cgo] go build -o ccgo.bin .
[cgo] exec ./ccgo.bin
[cgo] stdout '^ccgo: 42$'
[cgo] grep 'cc-wrapper' $WORK/cc.log
[cgo] ! exists $WORK/zig.log

-- go.mod --
module example.com/ccgoenv

go 1.27

-- main.go --
package main

/*
int answer() { return 42; }
*/
import "C"

import "fmt"

func main() { fmt.Println("ccgo:", C.answer()) }

-- $WORK/fakebin/zig --
#!/bin/sh
# Fake zig for the M0-S5 zig-fallback attack. It logs zig's argv, strips
# zig's leading "cc -target <triple>", and delegates the remaining C
# compiler arguments to the real C compiler at an absolute path, so the
# build finishes without needing PATH.
echo "zig $@" >>"${ZIGLOG:-$WORK/zig.log}"
if [ "$#" -lt 3 ]; then
	echo "fake zig: expected 'cc -target <triple>' arguments, got: $@" >&2
	exit 1
fi
shift 3
IFS= read -r real <"$WORK/realcc.txt"
if [ -z "$real" ]; then
	echo "fake zig: no pre-narrowing compiler recorded in $WORK/realcc.txt" >&2
	exit 1
fi
PATH=$REALPATH exec "$real" "$@"

-- $WORK/ccwrap/cc --
#!/bin/sh
# CC wrapper for the M0-S5 go-env-CC attack. It logs its argv, then execs
# the real C compiler recorded before PATH narrowed.
echo "cc-wrapper $@" >>"${CCLOG:-$WORK/cc.log}"
IFS= read -r real <"$WORK/realcc.txt"
if [ -z "$real" ]; then
	echo "cc wrapper: no pre-narrowing compiler recorded in $WORK/realcc.txt" >&2
	exit 1
fi
PATH=$REALPATH exec "$real" "$@"
